pr_title: fix(harness): write bookmark notes in the main session
verdict: READY TO MERGE - 5 of 5 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: The contract tests read the real SKILL.md and import the real add_note.py. The limits (MAX_NOTES, MAX_NOTE_CHARS) come from the script's own constants rather than copied literals, so the prose and the code cannot drift apart without a failure. Nothing is mocked.

test_skill_runs_the_script_through_the_launcher_with_each_subcommand pins the exact launcher form required by the project rule (sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/hpy" "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/..."). It also checks that every subcommand appears as 'NOTE <sub>' in the skill.
Keeping _AGENT as a path whose absence is checked means the test source still names bookmark-noter.md. tools/select_tests.py therefore selects the test on any diff that adds or deletes that file.

The tracker.test.ts background-launch case was moved to an agent that still exists (todo-editor), so it stays consistent with DEFINED_AGENTS. The model_family assertion depends on the usage model and not on the agent's frontmatter.

DEFINED_AGENTS in plugins/pr-review-watch/hooks/contract.ts now matches the seven files under plugins/harness/agents exactly (bookmark-noter removed with its agent file), so the docstring claim that the test pins the list to the agents folder holds.
The remaining entries keep alphabetical order, and the doc comment above the list still describes the code accurately.

SKILL.md matches add_note.py: the 20-note and 300-character limits, the `add_note: <reason>` exit-1 stderr line, the `note N/20: <line>` output, the add/list/clear subcommands and the cwd default for `--repo` all agree with the script.

Removing `model`, `context: fork` and `agent` from the frontmatter, deleting bookmark-noter.md and moving its procedure into the skill body leave no stale references; the only leftover name is the contract test, which asserts the agent file is gone.
The README overview row and the add-bookmark section both drop the 'Bash-only haiku agent' wording and say the session writes the note, consistent with the skill body.
The rule that a note gets only facts the conversation established, with no extra commands run, keeps the note free of side effects now that it runs in the main session.
The root cause is fixed rather than worked around: a forked haiku agent could never resolve 'the current status', so the skill now runs where the facts live, and the README says so plainly.
DEFINED_AGENTS in contract.ts and the tracker test drop bookmark-noter together; test_pr_review_watch_usage_contract globs plugins/*/agents, so the removal is checked against the files on disk.
test_skill_runs_in_the_main_session asserts that context, agent and model are absent, with a failure message explaining why, so a reflexive re-add of `model: haiku` fails loudly.
The launcher line follows the project convention (`hpy` plus `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`) and is pinned verbatim by the contract test; limits are still tied to add_note.py constants rather than literals.
Both changed plugins get a version bump; the removed agent leaves no stray references outside archived review JSON.

minor.name: New README bullet sits apart from the add-bookmark notes list
minor.summary: README.md lines 130-132 add a bullet followed by a blank line (133) before the existing bullets at 134-139. The blank line makes it one list, but a loose one, so every item in the add-bookmark notes gets paragraph spacing, unlike the other skill sections. In the raw file the new bullet also looks like a separate block.
fix: Delete the blank line at README.md:133 so the new bullet joins the existing list as a tight list

minor.name: Unescaped pipes split the usage row of the action table
minor.summary:
SKILL.md line 39 puts `usage: /harness:add-bookmark <note> | --list | --clear` inside a two-column GFM table. GFM splits cells on every unescaped pipe, code spans included, so the rendered row reads 'print `usage: /harness:add-bookmark <note>' with a dangling backtick and drops '--list', '--clear` and stop'. The raw text the session reads is intact, but anyone reading the skill on GitHub sees a truncated instruction. The deleted agent avoided this by keeping the usage line outside its table.

Also (roast): SKILL.md:39 puts `usage: /harness:add-bookmark <note> | --list | --clear` in the Action column of a GFM table. Pipes split table cells even inside a code span, so the rendered row has four cells and a broken code span. The deleted bookmark-noter.md avoided this on purpose: it said 'reply with the usage line below' and printed the line under the table, which was the fix recorded in the PR 56 review. This PR brings the old bug back while moving the text.
fix: Change the table cell to 'print the usage line below and stop' and add a line after the table: Usage line: `usage: /harness:add-bookmark <note> | --list | --clear`
Escape the pipes as `\|` inside the cell (the session then sees the backslashes in the raw text and could print them, so moving the line out of the table is the safer option)

Change the row to `| nothing | print the usage line below and stop |` and add `Usage line: `usage: /harness:add-bookmark <note> | --list | --clear`` as a plain line under the table, as the deleted agent did.
Or escape the pipes in the cell: `usage: /harness:add-bookmark <note> \| --list \| --clear`.

minor.name: 'Stays as written' conflicts with the quoting and length rules
minor.summary: SKILL.md:51 says text that already stands alone 'stays as written', but SKILL.md:54 requires rewording any line that contains a single quote, backtick or `$`, and add_note.py refuses more than 300 characters. A self-contained note such as `don't touch $HOME config` has to change. The model has to decide which rule wins, and the README (line 132) repeats the absolute version. Three rules, one of them absolute.
fix: Reword SKILL.md:51 to: `Text that already stands alone stays as written, apart from the quoting rule and the 300-character limit below.` and README.md:132 to `... is stored as written, apart from quoting and length.`

minor.name: Leftover note-writer answer text in the todo-editor background-launch test
minor.summary: The rename from harness:bookmark-noter to harness:todo-editor (lines 455, 464) left the loop turn's answer as 'noted' (line 459). That is a remnant of the note-writing agent. The test asserts nothing about the answer, so behavior is unaffected, but the fixture now reads as if the TODO editor wrote a bookmark note.
fix: Change answer: 'noted' at line 459 to a neutral value such as answer: 'done'.

minor.name: The guard against a context-free agent covers only frontmatter and one deleted filename
minor.summary:
The module docstring (lines 3-5) says the test pins 'that the skill never hands the note to a context-free agent'. Only two checks back that claim. test_skill_runs_in_the_main_session (44-48) rejects the frontmatter keys context/agent/model, and test_no_context_free_noter_agent_remains (51-52) checks that the single path agents/bookmark-noter.md is gone. A SKILL.md body that told the session to dispatch an agent with the Agent tool (for example 'dispatch harness:todo-editor with the note'), or a re-added noter agent under another name, would pass every test. So the docstring promises more than the code checks.

Also (tests): Line 48 fails each of context, agent and model with the message '{key} would run the note writer without the session's context'. That is true of context: fork and agent, which fork into a fresh agent. A skill-level model override switches the model for the skill's turn and keeps the main conversation. The ban on model may be intended, because a smaller model resolves session references less well, but the failure message gives the wrong reason. A maintainer who reads it may drop the key from the tuple or work around it.

Also (roast): test_no_context_free_noter_agent_remains (tests/skills/test_add_bookmark_skill_contract.py:51-52) only checks that `agents/bookmark-noter.md` does not exist. An agent restored under any other name that runs add_note.py would pass. The docstring promises more: 'the skill never hands the note to a context-free agent'. The frontmatter test at :44-48 already covers the skill side, so this test checks a path and nothing else.
fix: Add a body check to test_skill_runs_in_the_main_session: assert re.search(r'harness:(?!add-bookmark )[a-z-]+', _text(_SKILL)) is None and assert 'subagent' not in _text(_SKILL).lower(), so the skill body names no agent to dispatch.
Or narrow the docstring at lines 4-5 to what is checked: 'and that the skill does not fork (no context/agent/model frontmatter) and the bookmark-noter agent is gone'.

Split the check: keep the loop over ('context', 'agent') with the current message, and add a separate assert 'model' not in meta with a message such as 'model would hand note writing to a different model than the session's'.
Or drop 'model' from the tuple if a model override is acceptable for the skill.
Replace it with a scan: for every `plugins/*/agents/*.md`, assert that `add_note.py` does not appear in the text, so no agent can take over the note writer under any name.
Or delete the test and keep test_skill_runs_in_the_main_session as the guard.
